versions.rationale: One patch bump for focused skill-content changes; no other version fields exist in this package and no shared generated files changed.

baseline.inspection: All four owned files inspected completely. Scoped status/diff/cached diff empty at assignment. No nested AGENTS.md. Exact assignment content and SHA-256 snapshot retained for attribution.

findings.location: SKILL.md workflow overflow decision; references/flow-control-choices.md callback-to-prefetch boundary
findings.finding: The skill covered per-subscription budgets and callback demand but did not make the shared fan-out loss decision concrete. A sink's successful emission could be mistaken for delivery to every consumer.
findings.evidence: Reactor 3.7.5 Sinks.EmitResult explicitly does not guarantee consumption. directBestEffort may return OK while a subscriber with no demand misses the item; directAllOrNothing fails that attempt with FAIL_OVERFLOW in the controlled asymmetric-demand case.
findings.consequence: Changing the sink factory can change which consumers lose an item without establishing lossless delivery; producer success metrics can hide per-consumer gaps.
findings.resolution: Added a core per-consumer loss/acknowledgement guard, an explicitly routed shared-sink section, actual-factory/result inspection, a focused comparison table, no-replay semantics and choices conditional on delivery requirements.

findings.finding: A producer's emission API changes the failure path: rejected tryEmitNext and emitNext with FAIL_FAST cannot be treated as interchangeable failure reporting.
findings.evidence: Versioned InternalManySink.emitNext implementation and executed controlled checks show overflow becomes terminal through emitNext(value, FAIL_FAST), while tryEmitNext reports failure and remains usable in the tested direct variants.
findings.consequence: A proposed visibility fix can accidentally turn individual rejected events into termination of the shared stream.
findings.resolution: Explain the API distinction, separate capacity failure from serialization contention, and require tests of the chosen API and consumer sequences.

changes.detail: Added two lines at the overflow-policy decision and refined the existing reference reading condition for a slow subscriber on a shared sink.
Added one conditional multicast section and four versioned primary-source links; no new shipped resource or validation framework.

preserved: Reactor 3.7.5/core-micrometer 1.2.5 authoring baseline; Java 8+ core partial examples, Java 11+ JFR and Java21+ virtual-thread conditions.
Real request semantics and batching units, limitRate versus backlog bounds, local overflow and two-argument delayed drain/error behavior.
Callback create/push producer/demand differences and per-subscription listener cleanup.
flatMap lifetime/per-subscription limits, shared resource budgets, groupBy progress cycles, deferred blocking invocation and cancellation versus actual work termination.
Discard ownership, bounded producers and durable-transfer limits, no mandatory concurrency-model migration.
Micrometer names/types, missing-series interpretation, JFR event lifecycle, BlockHound coverage/compatibility and incident guidance.
Existing role, descriptions, dependencies and suggests. references/instrumenting-backpressure.md is byte-identical.

+## Shared sinks and a slow subscriber
+
+For manual fan-out, inspect the actual `Sinks.Many` factory, emission method/result handling
+and each consumer's demand. In Reactor 3.7.5, these direct multicast variants behave differently
+when one subscribed consumer has demand and another has zero demand, without cancellation races:
+
+| Factory after `Sinks.many().multicast()` | `tryEmitNext(value)` outcome | Consumer observation |
+| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------- |
+| `directBestEffort()`                    | `OK`                        | Only the consumer with demand receives this value |
+| `directAllOrNothing()`                  | `FAIL_OVERFLOW`              | Neither consumer receives this value |
+
+Both direct variants have no replay: requesting later does not recover that missed value.
+With subscribers but no demand anywhere, both return `FAIL_OVERFLOW`; with no subscribers,
+both return `FAIL_ZERO_SUBSCRIBER`. Handle the result according to the producer's ownership
+and loss contract. Ignoring a failure does not retain or retry the value. `EmitResult.OK`
+describes emission state, not completed processing or durable acceptance; cancellation can
